findings.what: The status cell says "18 call sites took an explicit epoch". Measured against HEAD: there were exactly 18 two-arg `new CommitLog(store, prefix)` sites in 5 files, but only 17 of them took an explicit epoch -- the 18th (CommitLogTest.java:247, inside `theTwoArgConstructorIsEpochZeroSoEveryExistingCallSiteKeepsItsMeaning`) was deleted with the test, as the very next sentence of the same cell says. The enumeration in the cell does not reconcile either: 11 predicted CommitLogTest sites + SubscriptionHubTest (1) + EndToEndTest (2) + two ITs (2) = 16, not 18; the true CommitLogTest count was 13 (12 converted plus the one in the deleted test).
findings.failure_scenario: A later agent auditing whether the constructor deletion was complete -- the usual check before, say, re-adding a convenience overload or grepping for stragglers -- takes 18 as the number of conversions, counts 17 in the commit, and either re-opens M4.6f as unfinished or concludes some call site was silently dropped, when the tree in fact holds zero two-arg sites and one three-arg constructor.

findings.what: The cell describes the two clusterTest ITs as "two `clusterTest` ITs, which no default test task compiles". `./gradlew test` indeed does not, but buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/binjava.java-conventions.gradle.kts ends with `tasks.named("check") { dependsOn("compileIntegrationTestJava", "compileClusterTestJava") }`, with a comment saying exactly why: "otherwise broken integration- or cluster-test code commits green". check-module.sh runs `:plugin:build`, so the two IT conversions in this diff WERE compile-checked by a gate that ran.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent reading this row later believes clusterTest sources are outside every default gate, changes an IT without compiling it (or skips updating one during a future API removal), and is surprised when `check-module.sh` fails at commit time -- or, worse, argues that a clusterTest breakage is acceptable to land because "no default task compiles it", weakening the compile coverage the conventions file deliberately bought.
